prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: [val2][adversarial] Incident IDs vs prose (language en).
Grid: 4 columns × 4 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 13px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Incident" · longest unbreakable word 68px · one-line width 127px
  col 2: header "Trace ID" · longest unbreakable word 245px · one-line width 245px
  col 3: header "Severity" · longest unbreakable word 52px · one-line width 52px
  col 4: header "Summary" · longest unbreakable word 65px · one-line width 612px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 735px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 734px.
Fixed: content, font, 13px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Connect each incident and its trace identifier to a severity and a brief description of the problem.","reading":"Readers can scan severity and summary for incidents of interest, then use the incident and trace IDs to locate or investigate a specific record.","groups":["Incident and Trace ID identify the same record and support lookup.","Severity and Summary describe the incident and support triage."],"keep_intact":["Trace IDs should remain intact where possible, since they are long, unbroken identifiers.","Incident IDs should remain intact where possible so they are easy to recognize and copy.","Severity codes should remain on one line."],"may_wrap":["Summary prose can wrap naturally between words; its line count will largely determine row height.","Incident IDs can wrap at hyphens if more space is needed for summaries.","Trace IDs may require forced breaking in a prose-first design."]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r1A: widths [148, 266, 73, 247] · table 735×214px · row heights [33, 73, 53, 53] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1B: widths [148, 220, 73, 293] · table 735×214px · row heights [33, 73, 53, 53] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 1
Design r1C: widths [130, 220, 73, 311] · table 735×214px · row heights [33, 73, 53, 53] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 1

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
